title: Simulating, Fast and Slow: Learning Policies for Black-Box Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2406.04261v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Simulators are vital in science and engineering, as they faithfully model the influence of design parameters on real-world observations. Optimizing design parameters to minimize a desired objective function is notoriously challenging since simulators are often non-differentiable black boxes. Moreover, each simulation incurs significant compute time, thus doing such optimizations naively may be prohibitively expensive. Furthermore, in experiment design settings, practitioners are typically required to solve the same optimization problem for various input distributions before proceeding to real-world experiments. Starting these related optimizations from scratch each time can be inefficient if the forward simulation model is expensive to evaluate. translated_title: 快与慢的模拟：面向黑盒优化的策略学习
translated_abstract: 模拟器在科学和工程中至关重要，因为它们忠实地建模了设计参数对真实世界观测的影响。优化设计参数以最小化期望的目标函数是出了名的困难，因为模拟器通常是不可微分的黑盒。此外，每次模拟都需要大量的计算时间，因此天真地进行此类优化的代价可能高得令人望而却步。而且在实验设计的场景中，从业者通常需要在进行真实世界实验之前，针对各种不同的输入分布求解同一个优化问题。如果前向模拟模型的评估成本很高，每次都从头开始进行这些相关优化就会非常低效。为了应对这些挑战，本文提出了一种新颖的方法，通过学习一个策略来引导……（摘要内容在此处被截断）……
tldr: 本文提出一种新方法，通过学习一个策略来引导在各种输入分布下的黑盒优化求解，避免了每次从头开始的昂贵模拟优化，从而大幅提升实验设计中优化的效率。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a novel method that learns a policy to solve black-box optimization problems across various input distributions, avoiding costly from-scratch optimizations with expensive simulators and greatly improving efficiency in experiment design.
